Question: Is there any promotional campaign that backfired?
Answer: In the Philippines during the early 1990s, Pepsi ran a promotion where numbers printed under bottle caps could win cash prizes. Pepsi Philippines (PCPPI) announced that they would print numbers, ranging from 001 to 999, inside the caps (crowns) of Pepsi, 7-Up, Mountain Dew and Mirinda bottles. Certain numbers could be redeemed for prizes, which ranged from 100 pesos (about US$4) to 1 million pesos. However, when the winning numbers were announced, it turned out a glitch had printed it on 800,000 bottle caps rather than two. This could have cost the company $32 billion, had it agreed to the requisite payouts - but it did not. Instead, it offered a much smaller amount to anyone who had the winning number, and while some accepted it (costing Pepsi $10 million), others did not.

Question: Why do doctors wear green clothes while performing an operation?
Answer: You must have seen that just before surgery, doctors get ready in green-coloured clothes. And we have all wondered at least once: why only green, and not any other colour? There is science behind it: a) When you enter a dark room from a place full of light, and if you come into contact with green or blue, you feel better. The doctors in the operating room go through the same thing. b) The green and blue colours are opposite to red on the spectrum of light; and during operation, the attention of the surgeon is mostly focused on red colours only. The green and blue colours of the cloth not only enhance a surgeon’s ability to see but also make him more sensitive to red. c) Doctors frequently don blue and white uniforms too. But because blood spots appear brown on it, the colour green is preferred. There is no clear explanation for why doctors wear blue or green uniforms. In the past, doctors and all hospital staff wore white uniforms.

Question: What do you think, is Iron Dome effective or useless? How does the Iron Dome actually work?
Answer: Iron Dome missile defense system…….How does it work? The Iron Dome was specially designed to protect against a range of incoming short-range threats. Basically, it has three components, which is the case for most air defense systems: radar that detects the incoming rocket; a command-and-control system that processes that information and then activates the third component, which is the interceptor — basically a missile whose role is to destroy the other rocket. Is Iron dome effective? The all-weather system was specially designed to help combat shorter-range weapons like the rockets fired from Gaza. The Iron Dome uses radar to identify and then intercepts & destroys the incoming threats before they can cause damage. More than 2,000 rockets have been fired towards Israel by Hamas and other Palestinian militant groups in five days. But about 90% of the rockets have been intercepted by Israel’s flagship Iron Dome missile defense system. Can it be relied upon completely? Iron Dome can detect and intercept anything, but it was designed for unsophisticated weapons like rockets. It cannot intercept ballistic missiles coming from Iran. So that’s the reason why it is effective technically — but strategically, it doesn’t change the fact that the Israelis cannot rely on it completely. Not saying that the Iron Dome is useless, I just think it’s like an insurance option. It’s a great way to reassure the citizens, also to avoid total disruption of daily life. But at the end of the day, this cannot be the only option. Iron Dome is considered among the most advanced defense systems in the world.

However, they were not able to come up with an explanation for this. In their search for answers, the US scientists also examined the birth rates in earlier centuries and came to the conclusion that always during and after a war, more boys than girls were born. The FOUR Monument is a place in the United States where you can be in four states at once! The monument itself is centered around a bronze disk that marks the exact point where the four state borders come together. The state boundaries marked by the monument have their origins in the period just before and during the American Civil War, when the United States Congress acted to form governments in the area to stop the spread of slavery in the region. Initially, these boundaries were defined using meridian and parallel lines and despite some initial errors, these markers became the legally recognized boundaries, overriding the written descriptions of meridians and parallels. This includes the Four Corners Monument, which is legally established as the intersection point of four states. The monument features a central granite disk with a smaller bronze disk at its center, surrounded by smaller state seals and flags representing both the states and the tribal nations of the region. The disk has an inscription that shows the border lines for each state, as well as a phrase that reads differently depending on where you start: “Four states here meet in freedom under God’, “Here meet in freedom under God four states”, “Under God four states here meet in freedom” or “In freedom under God four states here meet.” The Four corners attract many tourists despite their remote and isolated location.

Question: If the Big Bang expanded in all directions, then is the big bang the center of the universe?
Answer: The idea that the Big Bang is the center of the universe is a common misconception and misunderstanding of the Big Bang theory. The “Big Bang”, started at one point. But that point contained everything; “ALL Space and time.” All of space at one point, and everything compressed… it was produced in the entire universe at once. The “Big Bang Theory” explains how the universe has expanded and evolved since its inception approximately 13.8 billion years ago. According to this theory, the entire universe originated from a hot, dense spot and has been expanding in all directions ever since. But this does not mean that the Big Bang is the center of the universe, but that it occurred throughout the universe at the same time. Also, the universe is infinitely large, so it does not have a physical center. The expansion of the universe does not occur relative to a central point, but is a uniform expansion in all directions. For this reason, it cannot be said that the Big Bang is the center of the universe.

A monument in memory of Queen Huh is built on the banks of River Saryu in Korean tradition using a three-meter-high stone weighing 7,500 kg. South Korean Ambassador in India Chang Jae-Bok Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday said: "Ayodhya is very important for both of us historically. "I don't know if Ayuta is Ayodhya, but it's Ayuta in Korean language. It is generally assumed that Ayuta was Ayodhya or Ayodhya was Ayuta." He noted that the central government should share the program details around the Ram temple's inauguration for it to receive full assurance of high-level participation from foreign countries. Question: What are some of the most amazing human rescues?
Answer: NASA and ‘The 33’ Chilean Miners Year: 2010 Country: Chile Estimated Cost: $22 Million In 2010, all eyes were on 33 miners trapped for more than two months under the stone walls of a Chilean copper mine as the world watched and hoped for their safe rescue. Men and women from all over the world provided aid as the Chilean government sought assistance from other organizations for how to help the trapped miners. Among them was a team from NASA who provided insight from the agency’s long experience protecting humans in the hostile environment of space. It was 17 days after the main ramp’s collapse that contact with the miners was initiated, and another 52 days before they would be rescued from their underground prison. For the capsule itself, NASA engineers recommended exterior rollers and a trap door in the bottom. The rollers would cushion the ride up, reduce friction with tunnel walls, and lessen the possibility the capsule would get stuck midway, while the trap door allowed the rider to exit the capsule through the bottom and repel back down in case it got stuck midway. A twin capsule was built to enable teams to work through engineering problems that might occur during the rescue. To ensure the miner’s health on the way up, engineers provided other ideas, including an oxygen tank for an emergency air supply, an audio/video feed for communication with the rider during the transit, and medical probes like heart monitors so rescue teams could check vital signs during the rescue. Approximately $22 million was spent on the rescue that involved hundreds of people and drilling a human-sized hole hundreds of feet through solid rock. All 33 Chilean Miners were rescued safely.

Question: Is the moon a physical rock that we can land on or is it just a light?
Answer: The Moon is not a "light glow," but rather a natural satellite that orbits the Earth. The Moon reflects sunlight, which is why it appears to glow in the night sky. When astronauts land on the Moon, they are landing on its solid surface, not on light itself. Think of it like this: when you see the Moon from Earth, you're seeing sunlight that's being reflected off the Moon's surface back to your eyes. Just like how you can stand on the Earth's surface even though it's illuminated by sunlight, astronauts can land on the Moon's surface because it's solid ground that reflects the light.

Question: What is the biggest achievement of the Modi government so far?
Answer: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday announced that India and France have agreed to use Unified Payments Interface (UPI) payment mechanism and it will begin from the iconic Eiffel Tower. Addressing the Indian community at the La Seine Musicale, a performing arts center on an island in river Seine, PM Modi said that Indian tourists in France will now be able to make payments in rupees. “In France, an agreement has been made for the use of India’s UPI…It will be started from the Eiffel Tower, and now Indian tourists would be able to make payments in Rupees, through UPI, in the Eiffel Tower,” the prime minister said. In 2022, the National Payments Corporation Of India (NPCI), the umbrella organisation that offers UPI services, signed an MoU with France’s fast and secure online payment system, called Lyra. In 2023, UPI and Singapore’s PayNow signed an agreement, allowing users in either country to make cross-border transactions. The UAE, Bhutan, and Nepal have already adopted the UPI payment system. The NPCI international is in talks to extend the UPI services in the US, European countries, and West Asia. The UPI is indeed a revolution by India in the banking system. Barring the criticism of this government on various issues, this one is really progressive. Taking it to global is one of the great achievements by this Govt.

Question: What are some unique and exquisite national parks of India?
Answer: National Parks in India are certainly wonderful for wildlife buffs to scout the engrossing exquisiteness of nature. All the protected regions in the country have beautiful vistas to offer. Some arresting national parks in India that sets them apart are: 1) Hemis National Park, Jammu and Kashmir Hemis National Park is a high-altitude national park located in eastern Ladakh region of Jammu and Kashmir. There are around 200 snow leopards in the region and witnessing them amid the fascinating snowy panorama gives great pleasure. 2) Sundarbans National Park, West Bengal Sundarbans National Park is a national park, biosphere reserve and tiger reserve located in West Bengal, India. Sunderban is one of the largest reserves for tigers. It boasts around 400 tigers. 3) Keibul Lamjao National Park, Manipur Perched in the beautiful state of Manipur, Keibul Lamjao National Park stretches over 40 square kilometers of floating vegetation. It is the largest freshwater lake in the country. The park has a 1.5-meter-deep vegetation, which keeps floating. 4) Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch The Marine National Park is located seawards from the southern coastline of the Gulf of Kutch. The park is spread over an area of 458 square kilometers. It comprises a set of 42 islands. This national park is the first marine wildlife sanctuary and the first marine national park of India. 5) Namdapha National Park, Arunachal Pradesh Namdapha National park, located in Arunachal Pradesh, is the largest protected region of the Eastern Himalayan Biodiversity Hotspot. Area wise, Namdapha is the third largest national park of India. According to botanists, it will take around 50 years to complete a research on its varied botanical diversity. The distinctive traits of the above-mentioned national parks make them perfect destinations for enjoying an out of the box vacation. Their uniqueness makes them a blistering hot attraction among the wildlife freaks and nature buffs!

Question: What is an unusual and mysterious village in India?
Answer: A unique village in Kerala where human photocopies are found, literally. There is a village Kodinhi in Malappuram district in Kerala, where the birth rate of twins is probably the highest in India. At first glance, Kodinhi seems quite normal. Like many other villages in Kerala, it is lined with coconut palms, crisscrossed with canals and dotted with rice fields. But, when you go deeper into its narrow streets, you come across a large number of identical faces. This village Kodinhi about 150km from Kochi, Kerala has a total population of 2000, and more than 400 of them are twins. In such a situation, you will see many lookalike children, in the school and in the nearby market in this village. Around the world average of 4 twins are born out of 1000 babies and in India 9 twins per 1000 births, but in this mysterious village, 45 babies are born out of 1000 babies. On average, it is the second in the world after Nigeria's Igbo-ora which is also called the "Twin Capital of the World" where 145 twins out of 1000 are born, and the first in Asia. Not just in India, researchers around the world are surprised by this village because there are over 400 twins here. It is believed that this place has got the blessings of God because twins are seen in very few cases, wherein in this village so many twins are born together. Many times, scientists have tried to investigate this rare phenomenon, but the answer still eludes them. This village is nothing short of a miracle in the medical world. Many eminent experts and researchers came here, but they could not find any reason. The Kerala village, which is now nicknamed the ‘twin town’, have proudly established the Twins and Kin Association (TAKA) to register and provide support for the twins of Kodinhi and their families.
